messages.subject: coverageCount output format
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Thank you for your work, I am a frequent user of featureCounts and now am interested in using the coverageCount utility to calculate a coverage profile for some RNA-seq samples, but so far I was unable to find any documentation on the program which explains the format of the resulting .bin files. Are these files supposed to be used with the subread package or can they be used similar to samtools' pileups?
Any help is greatly appreciated.

Kind regards,
René

messages.subject: Re: coverageCount output format
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rene,

The coverageCount utility summarises the number of reads mapped at each base on the reference genome, and writes the counts to binary files, each for a chromosome listed in the header of the SAM or BAM file. The binary files are then named as ${output_prefix}-${chro_name}.bin. For example, the file name is "myResults-chrX.bin" when the output_prefix is "myResult", and the chromosome is chrX. You can also specify the directory name in the output prefix.

Each of the binary files contains many 4-byte integer numbers (little endian encoded, as the default format for x86 or x86-64). The byte-offset in the file is the zero-base position on the chromosome, times four. For example, if we want to know the number of reads covering the base of chrX:10000001 (one-based), we first open "myResults-chrX.bin", then load the four bytes from the 40000000th byte to the 40000003rd byte in this file. The coverage is then calculated by byte_1 + 256 * byte_2 + 65536 * byte_3 + 16777216 * byte_4.

Please be very careful that the byte-wise offset of the integer in the file is calculated from the zero-based chromosomal position, but the chromosomal positions in the SAM/BAM files are one-based.

The coverageCount program can deal with the soft-clipping and exon-exon junctions that are reported in the Cigar strings. However, there is a known issue in the coverageCount program: when the cigar string contains deletions (e.g., "40M5D60M"), these deleted bases on the chromosome still receive counts from this read.

Cheers,

Yang

messages.subject: Re: Please describe the featureCounts summary
messages.body_plain:
Apologies for my late reply. Your explanations are mostly correct. Below are my answers to your questions:

- Multi-mapping

When --primary is specified, the -M option will be ignored, meaning that a primary alignment will always be counted no matter the read is multi-mapped or not.

- Chimera

Your explanation is correct.

- Secondary

Not assigned because the alignment was marked as a secondary alignment in the FLAG field. The '--primary' option need to be turned on to disable the counting for such alignments.

- Nojunction

Not assigned because the read is an exon-spanning read. This is related to the option '--countSplitAlignmentsOnly'.

Hope this helps.

Wei

messages.subject: feature request for featureCounts
messages.body_plain:
Besides the mapped read count values for each sample, the output of Subread's featureCounts currently includes values for only the attribute that is specified by the 'g' option (gene_id by default; when summarization is done at meta-feature level). Thus, the output will not include the 'gene_name' attribute value even if it is there in the GTF (annotation) file.

It will be good if the featureCounts provides a way to optionally include values for other attributes that are there in the GTF file. E.g., having 'gene_name' values in the featureCounts output will be helpful and time-saving.
